items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had seen at the Savoy ballroom with an orchestra known as the San Domingo Serenaders

ctx.x: Every U.S.O. unit had a number and name. Our group was known as Drum Boogie number 789. We arrived in Honolulu the next day and Bubbles Martin was not feeling well, and went to see a doctor at the Hickam Field Base Hospital. He was put in bed and we were told that we could have passes to go into the city. That was quite alright with me because I had heard so much about Honolulu's Hawaii and wanted to see what it was like, although I didn't expect to see the chicks in grass skirts and I didn't see any. We had no…

We were given a pass every day and the second night, we found a dance hall that had some jazz musicians playing there. The next night we had our instruments and jammed until the joint closed. There was an alto player with the band that looked exactly like a musician named Durante whom I had seen at the Savoy ballroom with an orchestra known as the San Domingo Serenaders and he played exactly the same style. But this fellow denied that he had ever been in the States at all and he was not a Hawaiian. But he was a…

I saw Pearl Harbour and Wakiki Beach and jammed every night until Bubbles was well enough to continue the voyage. The public of the club was made up of natives and they liked jazz very much. They were used to it and we had a ball. We left Honolulu for the Philippines. There were stops in Kwajalein, an island in the pacific ocean and Guam.
